title: From Individuals to Interactions: Benchmarking Gender Bias in Multimodal Large Language Models from the Lens of Social Relationship
abstract: arXiv:2506.23101v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Ensuring the trustworthiness of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) requires rigorous evaluation of gender bias, particularly in socially sensitive domains. Existing benchmarks primarily assess bias in isolated contexts and are less suited to capturing biases that emerge through interpersonal interactions. We introduce Genres, a benchmark for evaluating gender bias in MLLMs through the lens of social relationships in narrative generation. Grounded in Fiske's relational models theory, Genres comprises 1,440 multimodal narrative elicitation pairs spanning four fundamental relationship types, diverse social scenarios, and three age groups. Its dual-character generation tasks elicit socially situated interpersonal narratives and enable fine-grained assessment across multiple dimensions of gender bias. translated_title: 从个体到互动：从社会关系视角评估多模态大语言模型中的性别偏见
translated_abstract: 确保多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）的可信度需要对性别偏见进行严格评估，尤其是在社会敏感领域。现有基准主要评估孤立情境下的偏见，不太适合捕捉通过人际互动产生的偏见。我们提出了Genres，一个通过社会关系视角评估多模态大语言模型在叙事生成中性别偏见的基准。Genres基于Fiske的关系模型理论，包含1,440个多模态叙事引导对，涵盖四种基本关系类型、多样的社会场景和三个年龄组。其双角色生成任务能够引出处于社会情境中的人际叙事，并支持跨多个性别偏见维度的细粒度评估。在六个近期多模态大语言模型上的实验揭示了持续存在但强烈依赖于关系类型和模型的性别差异。
tldr: 提出了基于Fiske关系模型理论的Genres基准，通过1,440个双角色多模态叙事生成任务从社会关系视角评估多模态大语言模型的性别偏见，发现性别差异持续存在且高度依赖于关系类型和具体模型。
